current_example.title: Example: Finding the Radius or Diameter of a Sphere Given Its Volume

q-13256.name: Question 1
q-13256.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14234518/assets/cc3274e21594169662d7b96d0fcadbab1b78a3d944445cc84aad4d37b395bed6.png)

Determine the volume of the sphere above.
q-13256.worked_solution:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

$$
V=\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $r=1\,\text{in}$ into the formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\frac{4}{3}\pi (1)^{3}=\frac{4}{3}\pi \,{\text{in}}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-118335.name: Question 2
q-118335.problem: What is the volume of a sphere whose diameter is $8\,\text{mm}?$
q-118335.worked_solution:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

$$
V=\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $r=\frac{8}{2}=4\,\text{mm}$ into the formula, we obtain

$$
V=\frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {4}^{3}=\frac{256}{3}\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{3}.
$$

q-32616.name: Question 3
q-32616.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14234518/assets/26b1e5acba63b8ee11d35e12bf0c8fd6944b7a466c9eab258ef36f6429e8ec0a.png)

What is the radius of a sphere whose volume is $320\pi {\text{ cm}}^{3}?$
q-32616.worked_solution:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

$$
V=\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $V=320\pi \,{\text{in}}^{3}$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ 320\pi  & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ 320\pi \cdot \frac{3}{4\pi } & ={r}^{3} \\ {r}^{3} & =240.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
r=\sqrt[3]{240}=2\sqrt[3]{30}\,\text{cm}.
$$

q-32616.html:
Question 3
?

What is the radius of a sphere whose volume is 320π cm3?

a
363cm
b
230cm
c
630cm
d
3203cm
e
2303cm
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

V=43πr3,

where r is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting V=320πin3 into the formula, we get

V=43πr3320π=43πr3320π⋅34π=r3r3=240.

Therefore,

r=2403=2303cm.

q-33799.name: Question 4
q-33799.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14234518/assets/bf8bd7c7679e1c1df6c336b48892964c7658ac877b5efc22b099b1e98129d9ac.png)

What is the radius of a sphere whose volume is $\frac{343}{6}\pi \,{\text{ft}}^{3}?$
q-33799.worked_solution:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

$$
V=\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $V=\frac{343}{6}\pi \,{\text{ft}}^{3}$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \frac{343}{6}\pi  & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \frac{343\pi \cdot 3}{6\cdot 4\pi } & ={r}^{3} \\ {r}^{3} & =\frac{343}{8} \\  & =\frac{{7}^{3}}{{2}^{3}} \\  & ={(\frac{7}{2})}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
r=\sqrt[3]{{(\frac{7}{2})}^{3}}=\frac{7}{2}\,\text{ft}.
$$

q-33799.html:
Question 4
?

What is the radius of a sphere whose volume is 3436πft3?

a
72ft
b
112ft
c
103ft
d
2ft
e
73ft
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula V=43πr3, where r is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting V=3436πft3 into the formula, we get

V=43πr33436π=43πr3343π⋅36⋅4π=r3r3=3438=7323=(72)3.

Therefore, r=(72)33=72ft.
